title: [CQ-M06a] Promotion decision record
description:
Objective: Record the CQ rollout promotion decision honestly from the frozen baseline. Report the 50% planner and 30% retrieval targets and accepted-change cost/time/quality, decide promotion or non-promotion, and record unsupported hardware. This is a SPIDR slice of [CQ-M06] (task-ced857485a1c4d75b57cc25dcc9b4d82), which keeps the docs sweep, the full multi-package regression and the whole-epic review. It depends on CQ-M05, so every workstream's final certification state is known when it runs.

Deliverable:
- docs/baselines/cq-m06/README.md: the decision record. Every figure is derived from docs/baselines/cq-m04/report.json (M04c, n=1, 20 workloads, legacy workflow).
  - No matched pilot is run here, so every pilot figure, delta and target outcome reads 'unmeasured'.
  - Retrieval counters are unknown in all 20 baseline rows, so the 30% retrieval target is unmeasurable against this baseline.
  - The decision is non-promotion while assertExecutionProfileReady still refuses verified-local. The record lists each unmet gate: readiness, the VM/client/check capabilities CQ-M05 reports unsupported, the matched pilot and the retrieval baseline.
  - It gives each platform's support status, and states that skipped real-VM tests do not certify support.
- packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/rolloutDecision.test.ts: a guard test. It recomputes every quoted figure from report.json, pins the decision to the readiness authority, and requires the honesty statements.

Not in scope:
- Running any agent workload or a paid matched pilot. That needs a separate, explicitly approved batch that matches M04c's corpus, caps and role models, with retrieval counters in both arms.
- Enabling any profile.
- Changing the baseline/report scripts or the M04c archive.
- Any other doc: CQ-M06 sweeps them.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test
definitionOfDone: docs/baselines/cq-m06/README.md records non-promotion (verified-local stays disabled) and lists every unmet gate: readiness uncertified, unsupported VM/client/check capabilities, no matched pilot, unknown retrieval baseline.

It reports the 50% planner and 30% retrieval targets and accepted-change cost/time/quality. Each figure is derived from docs/baselines/cq-m04/report.json, unmeasured values read 'unmeasured' or 'unknown', and no savings are claimed.
It records each platform's support status and states that skipped real-VM tests do not certify support.

packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/rolloutDecision.test.ts fails in each of these cases, each proven by a scratch-copy mutation: a quoted figure drifts from report.json; a promotion is recorded while assertExecutionProfileReady refuses verified-local; a required statement is missing; a percentage other than the two targets appears.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits 0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.
No paid agent runs or pilot batches in this task: record the decision from existing evidence only.

implementationPlan.description:
Write docs/baselines/cq-m06/README.md: the decision record (~110 lines), from existing evidence only. No agent runs, no pilot (task rail).

Compute every figure first, with a throwaway `node -e` over docs/baselines/cq-m04/report.json that uses the guard's fmt and median rules. Paste the values verbatim and never round by hand.

Sections:
1. Title 'CQ rollout promotion decision', then a one-paragraph scope. It decides promotion of the strong profile (verified-local) from the CQ-M04c baseline (n=1, 20 workloads, legacy workflow, moe commit and corpus version as in report.json), and is not a savings or quality-improvement claim. Then the line 'Decision: non-promotion'.
2. '## Gates' table (Gate | Status | Evidence):
   - readiness: unmet. assertExecutionProfileReady refuses verified-local with EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY.
   - One row per CQ-M05 activationGaps() entry (vm, client, check), each with its exact reason: unsupported. The evidence column cites CQ-M05's PROJECT_SETTINGS_UPDATED refused-activation record.
   - matched pilot: unmet. Not run, because it needs a separately approved paid batch.
   - retrieval baseline: unmet. sourceRetrievals is unknown in all baseline rows.
3. '## Targets' table (Target | Baseline (CQ-M04c) | Pilot | Outcome):
   - '50% fewer planner invocations (target)': baseline is the mean planner sessions per workload and its observed count; pilot 'unmeasured'; outcome 'unmeasured'. Single-run workloads never re-enter PLANNING, and recipe activation is deferred, so a pilot of today's workflow could not show planner reuse.
   - '30% less repeated source retrieval (target)': baseline unknown in N of N rows; pilot 'unmeasured'; outcome 'unmeasurable against this baseline'.
4. '## Accepted-change cost, time and quality (baseline only)':
   - quality: accepted/rejected/notAssessed by the held-out assessment;
   - cost: observed tokens and tokens per accepted change, marked incomplete, with the reasoning tokens unknown;
   - 'Tokens are not monetary cost.';
   - time: the median end-to-end ms over the observed rows; first-code-change unknown in N rows;
   - 'Pilot: unmeasured.' and 'Claimed savings: none.'
5. '## Platform support' table (Platform | Status | Evidence). Take the rows from what R13 (task-f4811a72) and I06 (task-4e412148) LANDED (their completion summaries and Serena handoffs) and from probes on this host: `uname -a`, `command -v multipass`, `java -version`. Cover at least: WSL2 Linux (this host), Linux VM provisioning, Windows host, macOS and the IDE clients. Use only the statuses certified, not certified, unsupported and not run; certified only where landed real-hardware evidence says so. Then the line 'Skipped real-VM tests do not certify support.'
6. '## What a promotion needs': certified readiness, VM/client/check capabilities and hardware; a matched pilot on the same corpus digest, caps and role models, with retrieval counters in both arms (which means a re-run baseline); recipe activation; and quality no worse than the baseline. Each item is a separately approved task.
7. Links to docs/baselines/cq-m04/README.md and report.md.

Percent signs appear only in the two target rows. Error handling: if a figure cannot be derived (a field missing in report.json), write 'unknown' and make the guard expect it; never estimate.
Run the guard: it turns green.

One adversarial self-review of this task's diff only (load adversarial-self-review). Read the README as a skeptical reviewer looking for an unmeasured claim:
- Every number traces to a report.json field or a guard computation.
- No sentence implies savings, improvement, readiness, isolation or support beyond the cited evidence.
- Unknown counters say unknown, never 0.
- Platform rows cite landed R13/I06 evidence or a probe run on this host; skipped tests are never evidence.
- The pilot is described as not run, with what it would need.

Check the guard for brittleness: CRLF line endings, a README that is missing or empty, a report.json whose field is null, and an even-count median.

Error handling: the guard throws named errors and never passes on missing input.

Confirm there are no .moe edits, no Git writes and no changes to scripts/baseline-*.mjs or docs/baselines/cq-m04.

@governor-693b7073 Edge fix from architect-b58e1112, re-sent here because the chat copy (msg-8a87df81 in chan-18116c9a) was loop-guarded with no routing targets.

Dropping R13 (f4811a72), I06 (4e412148) and V12 (b621ddc9) from CQ-M05 removed the only thing holding back this row and M06. worker-c0a1ac70 has already claimed M05, so this row becomes claimable the moment M05 lands, before R13's operator reports and before I06 lands. - This row (M06a beb698a4): addDependsOn f4811a72 and 4e412148. Its step 2 builds the '## Platform support' table from what R13 and I06 LANDED.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. A decision script (scripts/rollout-decision.mjs) comparing baseline and pilot reports. Rejected (YAGNI): no pilot exists. A one-time decision record plus a guard test that recomputes its figures gives the same honesty guarantee at about half the code. A comparison builder belongs to the future pilot task.
2. A hand-written README with no guard. Rejected: DoD4 requires mutation-proven failure on figure drift, a promotion while not ready, missing statements, and extra percentages.
3. Running a matched pilot. Excluded by task rail. It also could not test either target: the baseline retrieval counters are null in 20 of 20 rows, and single-run workloads never exercise plan reuse (mem decision-cq-m06-split).
4. Guarding the platform rows against fixed expectations. Rejected: R13 and I06 own certification. The guard pins only the vocabulary and the honesty statement, and the M06 final step re-checks consistency.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Benchmark tests resolve REPO_ROOT relatively: src/benchmarks/non-routineWorkloads.test.ts:44.
- docs/baselines/cq-m04/README.md is the style precedent: plain facts, an explicit no-claims line, regeneration commands.
- report.json is schema version 1, with top keys version, inputs, rows, summary and limitations. Rows carry planning, retrieval, latency, usage and acceptance.
- The guard imports assertExecutionProfileReady from delivery/executionProfile.js (landed) and activationGaps from state/profileRollout.js (CQ-M05: an assumed name; adapt to what landed).
planningNotes.risks:
- Brittle figure formatting: use the guard's own fmt/median rules to produce the README values.
- CRLF working copies: split on /\r?\n/.
- The Linux gate needs a full archive that includes docs/.
- CQ-M06 (final) may later edit drifted README lines; the guard must keep passing.
- If CQ-M05's activationGaps is absent or renamed, adapt the import. If no gap source exists at all, report_blocked naming task-c53999b2. Never hard-code the gaps.
